name: Codex CLI
invoke: spawn the `waypost-<role>` agent, or `codex exec "$(waypost agents show <role>) <target>"`

skills.notes: Scans `.agents/skills` from the working directory up to the repository root, plus `$HOME/.agents/skills`; invoked as `$skill-name`. There is no `.codex/skills`.

notes: Codex has project-level agents now: .codex/agents/<name>.toml with name, description and developer_instructions (the system prompt), plus optional model, model_reasoning_effort and sandbox_mode. `sandbox_mode = "read-only"` is emitted, which is the one place a harness enforces the roles' read-only contract rather than asking for it. The older ~/.codex/prompts custom prompts are deprecated by OpenAI in favour of skills, so waypost no longer writes them; project agents need no follow-up copy step, so this entry has no after_install. `model_reasoning_effort` uses `{effort}` through `roles.effort.map`, which conservatively maps the neutral effort levels onto low/medium/high. Every shipped role is effort:max today, which this maps to "high"; revisit the map if Codex's own scale changes. On `detect`: AGENTS.md is kept deliberately, not by omission. A live session was measured on 2026-09-30 (codex-cli 0.159.2) and it creates no project-local .codex/ at all, while OpenAI's own docs/agents_md.md makes AGENTS.md the primary project instruction file discovered from the repository root — so in a real Codex project this path is often the only on-disk evidence there is. It is also the file all 21 entries read, so a project that keeps it for other tools is over-counted as a codex project; the cost is one extra `agents install`, and it is accepted deliberately rather than left undecided (see the setup-evidence ADR). The official subagents page confirms standalone project TOML files and the emitted name, description, developer_instructions and sandbox_mode fields. Verified live, 2026-09-30, codex-cli 0.159.2 on macOS: the runbook prerequisite setup --harness codex installed five project roles and ten skills into a throwaway Git project. A separate signed-in codex exec --approve-for-me session then executed all nine runbook steps without caller intervention. Its transcript independently loaded waypost-draft, waypost-story, waypost-commit and waypost-doctor. Outside checks confirmed commit 4c16f42 with Waypost-Harness: codex, Waypost-Session: codex-e-7310-a00f-9f9bb49ae338 and Waypost-Story: PS-1/story-hello-from-codex; the stored harness and proc.comm both name codex, and the live session held its story claim and README lease. Normal workspace-write protects .git metadata; the session autonomously retried story plan with scoped approval after the new failed-claim diagnostic. No blanket sandbox bypass was used. Doctor inside the sandbox had zero issues and one process-table warning; outside, zero issues and zero warnings, and the finished CLI session was correctly detected as ended. This verifies that configuration and platform, not Windows/Linux or every approval mode. The first independent run revealed a silent failed claim: story plan/close now report failed coordination while preserving the advisory gate. The parent tool initially supplied CODEX_THREAD_ID without CODEX_SESSION_ID; later probes supplied both with equal values. Subagents can inherit the parent session id and get a different thread id; existing session-id precedence is retained. Details and step evidence: docs/vault/ops/verify-a-harness-live-the-whole-waypost-loop-in-one-session.md.

inspect_model.notes: Returned runtime metadata only. Missing reasoning stays unknown; provider may be billing route.

coordination.notes: Owned ephemeral thread on a dedicated stdio app-server. Desktop socket/address delivery unverified; never attach implicitly.
